title: Computing Innovations, Input & Output
html:
AP Computer Science Principles

Computing
Innovations

Purpose, input & output

计算创新 · 程序目的 · 输入与输出
note: 从上一课的“信息怎样用位表示”转向“程序用这些信息做什么”。今天不要求写代码，目标是能把一个创新说清楚，并完成可检验的纸面设计。先用学生熟悉的校园找教室情境进入，不列举大量产品名称。

title: Retrieve before we move on
html:
1. Decode the unsigned binary integer 00101010.
  2. A label needs 20 distinct codes. What is the minimum bit length?
  3. Must 00101010 always mean a number?
Show answer
1. 42 = 32 + 8 + 2.
2. 5 bits: 16 < 20 ≤ 32.
3. No. An agreed encoding can give the same pattern another meaning.
note: 独立作答90秒，同桌比较45秒，剩余时间揭晓并记录错因。第一题是位权，第二题是容量，第三题为本课数据意义做桥梁。第二题若答20位，请学生先列2的幂；若答4位，追问16个模式怎样给20项唯一编号。错误较多的学生课后先补L01，不把本课前半段变成重复讲授。

title: What you will be able to explain
html:
1. Explain an innovation’s purpose and its function.
  2. Identify data entering and leaving a program.
  3. Describe input → processing → output.
  4. Design for a user and state a checkable requirement.

为什么开发？做什么？数据从哪里来、到哪里去？
note: 让学生把purpose旁标“why”，function旁标“what it does”。最后目标是本课对设计的初步应用，不等于正式Create任务。请学生最后用一个完整情境展示四项目标，不以背四个定义代替理解。

title: What makes an innovation computational?
html:
A computing innovation uses a program as an essential part of what it does.

Physical example

A programmable robot adjusts its route using sensor data.

Software example

A music app lets users arrange sounds into a composition.

The purpose can solve a problem or support creative expression.
note: 先解释computing innovation不是“最新款电子产品”的同义词；判断时要指出计算程序在功能中发挥什么作用。机器人是实体例子，音乐创作软件说明创新也可以没有单独的新硬件。不要声称必须连网、有AI或必须商业成功。创新目的可包含兴趣、艺术和表达，游戏也可能是合适例子。此页使用课堂概括定义，官方对齐重点是CRD-2.A.1的目的。

title: Which examples qualify?
html:
Choose the computing innovations. Give evidence.

A. A hand-operated can opener

B. An app that remixes recorded sound

C. A paper room-booking chart

D. A programmed controller that waters plants using sensor readings

Show answer
B and D. B runs software to transform sound; D runs a program to use readings and control watering. The stated A and C do not use a program.
note: 先投票，再要求回答包含“哪个程序做了什么”。不要接受“因为它很智能”“因为它用电”这样的泛泛判断。A明确为手动开罐器，C明确为纸质表，所以不引出电动或电子版本的歧义。若学生提出自动浇水也可以不用软件，承认可能存在机械实现，再让他们回到题干的controller runs a program这一既定情境。

title: Purpose and function answer different questions
html:
A library room finder

Purpose · 为什么

Help students find a suitable study room with less searching.

Function · 做什么

Accept a group size, compare it with room data, and display suitable rooms.

Purpose explains the need; function describes the program’s behavior.
note: 本课主案例从现在开始贯穿。用两个句式支架：The purpose is to help [user] [goal]；The program takes [input] and [action] to produce [output]。这里function指整体功能，不指某种语言中的函数定义。程序功能可以概括叙述，今后读代码时再解释语句如何实现它。避免说目的和功能永远不能用同一动词，重点是解释角度和信息是否充分。

title: Repair a weak explanation
html:
“The purpose of the room finder is to display a list.”

  1. What does this statement leave unclear?
  2. Rewrite it for a student planning group study.
Show one strong response
It describes a feature but leaves the user’s goal unclear.
Improved purpose: Help students locate available rooms large enough for their study group.
note: 先让学生在原句划出可观察功能“display a list”，再追问为什么有人需要这个列表。接受不同但有证据的目的，如减少寻找合适房间的时间。不要把“display a list”判为事实错误；它是不够完整的目的说明。要求改写具体点名用户和目标，不把“make life easier”作为充分答案。

title: A program carries out instructions
html:
A program is a set of instructions executed by a computer to carry out a task.

Program

The room-finding software.

Data

The group size, room capacities and availability.

The instructions describe what to do; the data provide values to work with.
note: 用“规则与这次处理的材料”来区分程序和数据，但不把两者当作不同物质：上一课知道二者最终都可以用位表示。软件可由多个程序组成，课堂此处用software作为常见称谓。先给宽泛行为解释，不提前教语法、函数或代码片段。学生若问“房间表算程序吗”，回答本例中表是数据，比较和筛选规则属于程序行为。

title: Input is the data, not just the device
html:
Input is data sent to a program for processing.

SourceExample input data
UserA typed group size: 4
Device / sensorA room occupancy reading
FileA table of room capacities read from storage
Another programUpdated room availability

指出数据本身：不要只写 keyboard、sensor 或 file。
note: 依次追問“究竟哪条数据进入程序”。键盘是设备，数字4才是本例输入；传感器是来源，占用读数是数据。文件只有被程序读取时才作为这一处理过程的输入，不是磁盘上所有文件都自动成为输入。来源类别不一定互斥，例如另一程序也可能通过文件提供数据。这里的四行是具体课堂实例，不把它们说成CED规定的互斥分类体系。

title: Output can be seen, heard or felt
html:
Output is data a program sends to a device.

Visual / text
“Room B is available.”

Audio
A spoken room number.

Tactile · 触觉
A vibration alert.

Stored output
A results file written to storage.

Identify the information or signal produced, not only the screen or speaker.
note: 输出不等于只在屏幕显示文本。声音、触觉反馈和写入存储的结果都是可用例子，但每个例子都要说清程序发送了什么。振动涉及程序发送给设备的控制信号，物理感觉是学生观察到的表现。若用机器人例子，输出可说发往电机控制器的动作指令，而不是把机器人的全部物理运动都泛称数据。

title: Direction depends on the program boundary
html:
A sensor program sends “occupied” to the room finder.

Sensor program → “occupied” → Room finder

Is the message input, output, or both?

Show answer
It is output from the sensor program and input to the room finder. Name the program before you classify the direction.
note: 让两名学生各代表一个程序，一张卡片代表occupied消息，卡片离开甲进入乙。边界概念是本课高价值难点：同一数据可以在一处是输出、另一处是输入。不要让学生只写“both”就结束，要以from/to指出相对哪个程序。物理连接、协议和网络传输细节留后续课程。

title: Follow one complete run
html:
Request: a room for 4 students.

RoomCapacityAvailable now?
A2Yes
B6Yes
C8No

Keep available rooms with enough seats. Display every match.

Show answer
Input: 4 and the room table. Processing: check capacity and availability. Output: Room B.
note: 本页先只展示表格，让学生手动圈出每一步条件，暂不使用if语法。A有空却座位不足，C够大却不可用，B满足两个要求。强调表格也是程序读取的输入，不能只写学生键入的4。筛选是处理，Room B是输出；表中的Yes只是读入的状态数据，不因为在投影片上看得到就成为被分析程序的输出。

title: Connect bits to useful information
html:
A room device sends 00000110.

The specification says this is an unsigned binary integer giving the number of seats.

  1. What capacity does the room finder receive?
  2. Could the bits alone tell us whether the room is occupied?
Show answer
1. 6 seats: 4 + 2.
2. No. This specified field encodes capacity; it supplies no occupancy status.
note: 这是跨课迁移题：不要只奖励算出6，还要学生读specification。题干明确该字段表示座位数，所以不能自行把最低位当作occupied开关。追问同一6在天气编码里能否不同含义，以巩固上下文决定意义。此页无需讨论实际通信协议或字节序。

title: An event can supply input
html:
Some instructions run when a defined event occurs.

Room finder example

Clicking Search sends a click event to the program.

The search behavior is triggered by that event.

Identify another event

A user presses Enter in the group-size field.

Show answer
The key-press event supplies information about the key action.

event：事件。输入不只包括用户输入的文字。
note: 用点击Search和按Enter说明事件既关联动作又可提供输入数据；按钮标签不是“这次事件”。可以演示按一下鼠标但不要写事件处理代码。CED列举程序启动也能生成事件，因此不要说所有事件都必须来自人工点击。本课只建立触发执行概念；事件驱动与顺序控制的正式比较、实现细节后续程序课继续。

title: Why the same click can give a different result
html:
An app stores the number of completed tasks.

Stored count: 2

Click “Complete one” → displays 3

Stored count: 7

Click “Complete one” → displays 8

Why does an identical click produce a different number?

Show explanation
The output also depends on the program’s prior state: the stored count before the click.
note: 不要从“输入通常影响输出”推成“同一条当前输入永远同一输出”。本例完整解释差异来源是已有计数值，并非程序无规律或随机。state用“程序记住的当前值”解释即可，变量赋值与更新将在下一课展开。顺便提醒一项输入变化也不一定改变输出，例如两个不同组别都可能适合Room B。

title: Choose the purpose
html:
An app converts a reader’s selected text into speech.

Which statement best describes its purpose?

A. It receives selected text.

B. It produces an audio signal.

C. It helps users access written material by listening.

D. It uses program instructions.

Show answer
C. It explains the user goal. A and B describe input/output; D identifies an implementation feature.
note: 独立选择30秒，然后要求学生为另外三个选项贴input/output/program feature标签。C不是因为句子最长，而是它解释创新为什么有用。不要限定只有视障读者可以使用，通勤者、语言学习者等也可能受益；目的表述可以适当广泛，但要与题干功能对应。此题是原创AP风格练习，不标真题。

title: Select exactly two inputs
html:
A translation program reads a photo and a chosen target language, then displays translated text.

Which TWO are inputs to this program?

A. The photo data

B. The translated text it displays

C. The selected target language

D. The program’s instructions

Show both answers
A and C. B is output; D is the program that processes the supplied data.
note: 提醒必须选恰好两项，先判断每个选项再作答。照片是输入数据，不必是键盘文字。程序指令本身也以位存储，但题目划定的翻译程序中，它们负责处理，不是本次翻译请求提供的输入材料。不要引出编译器“代码也可作为另一程序输入”的例外，若学生主动问可肯定并指出边界不同。

title: Start with people, not a feature list
html:
Before designing the room finder, investigate:

  1. Who needs to find a room?
  2. What makes a room suitable for that person?
  3. What constraints could prevent them using the result?

Suggest one useful interview question.

Show an example
“Tell me about the last time you struggled to find a study room. What made the search difficult?”
note: 不要代替用户想当然地列二十项功能。提问最好收集经历与约束，少问“你喜欢我们的好点子吗”。可提及轮椅通行、噪声需求、设备屏幕和开放时间，但不要假定群体所有成员需求一致。结对活动中一人扮演用户只能产生初步反馈，不能代替真实调查。对齐F.1–3为预习，不把一次访谈等同完整开发流程。

title: Make success observable
html:
Too vague

“The app should be good and easy.”

Checkable requirement

For a group of 4, show every available room with at least 4 seats.

With our room table, what result would demonstrate this requirement?

Show answer
Only Room B. Room A has too few seats; Room C is unavailable.
note: 成功标准应把要求转为可观察结果。这里不用宽泛“用户觉得好”当作程序正确性证据；但可用真实用户任务完成情况评估易用性。教学生区分检查一次样例与证明所有情况正确：Room B例子只是一个测试。提醒真正的程序还要处理不同组大小和无匹配结果，本课设计时至少考虑一项变化。

title: Design a room finder on paper
html:
One designer + one user. Swap roles halfway.

  1. Write a purpose naming the user and their goal.
  2. Sketch one screen. Label input data and output data.
  3. Describe the processing in plain English.
  4. Write one input case and its expected result.
Show a possible design
Example: group size 4 + room table → keep available rooms with enough seats → display Room B. Purpose: help study groups find suitable space.
note: 先1分钟访谈用户需求，再2分钟画图并注明数据方向；3分钟时交换角色，后半完成处理规则和一个检查案例。屏幕不要求美观，信息流清楚更重要。巡堂看四件证据：用户目标、实际数据而非设备名、至少一个处理动作、可核对的预期结果。只有明确需要才增加一个约束，如安静区域；不要不断加功能导致无法完成。答案在学生产出后再展示。

title: Try to break the design, then revise it
html:
A group of 7 students tries the same room finder.

Room A: 2 seats, available. B: 6 seats, available. C: 8 seats, unavailable.

  1. What should the user see?
  2. Does your design specify this case? Revise it.
Show expected behavior
No room meets both conditions. Show “No suitable room available”; do not return a full or undersized room. Add this behavior if it is missing.
note: 用一个失败匹配情境检验学生是否把“总会有结果”作为隐含假设。程序应明确给出无匹配反馈；空白屏幕可能无法让用户分辨正在加载还是无结果。两人互换设计，用笔标出具体修改，并写“因为……所以改为……”一句。此活动展示根据反馈迭代的思路，既没有实现程序也没有全面测试，因此只能称CRD-2.E.3初步体验。

title: Homework & the next lesson
html:
Homework

12 original questions · about 40 minutes.

Q1–Q6: multiple choice.
Q7–Q12: explain, trace and design.

Check your explanations

Name the program boundary.

Name the actual data.

Connect the function to a user goal.

Next: turn a simple design into a program using values, variables and sequence.
note: 布置Homework标签页的12题，提醒Q5选两项全部选对才得1分，书面题4分为教师练习评分，并非官方Create或FRQ评分表。要求先独立作答再对照答案；答案卷包含干扰项解释。Q1、Q2会回顾L01，不因进入新内容就停止提取旧知识。下一课开始写简单程序；本课纸面设计可用作引入，但不要求学生课前自行实现。

title: Exit ticket: explain a new situation
html:
A music app records a user’s tapping and plays a matching drum rhythm.

  1. State one plausible purpose.
  2. Identify one input, naming the data.
  3. Identify one output, naming the data or signal.
  4. Is “plays a drum rhythm” a purpose or a function description?
Show answer
1. Help users create or explore rhythms.
2. Tap timing / tap-event data.
3. The drum audio signal sent to speakers.
4. A function description.
note: 独立3分钟，最后2分钟揭晓并快速收集结果。四题各1分，purpose需说明创作或兴趣目标，input需比“screen”更具体，output需比“speaker”更具体。建议3/4且输入输出都正确可继续；若输入输出混淆，下一课先用箭头卡片补练。第一题有多个合理目的，按是否与行为相容而不是是否照抄标准答案评分。诊断标准是教师建议，不是AP官方量表。
